> 道沖，而用之或不盈。

Chapter 4 describes the Dao with the one image the rest of the book keeps returning to: a vessel that never fills.

沖 is not "empty" as a negation. It is the state of a container whose capacity has not been used up — the hollow that keeps the thing usable. 用之或不盈: use it, and it still does not brim over. Not because nothing is poured in, but because the hollow is not a fixed volume.

## Two halves

The chapter splits cleanly. The first half looks up: 淵兮，似萬物之宗 — deep, seemingly the ancestor of the ten thousand things. The second half looks down and becomes instruction:

> 挫其銳，解其紛，和其光，同其塵.

Four verbs, four operations on the self:

- 挫其銳 — blunt the sharp edge. Not dull yourself into incompetence; take the edge off the part that cuts first and thinks later.
- 解其紛 — untangle the knot. The tangle is usually not in the situation but in the several claims you have stacked on it.
- 和其光 — temper the glare. Whatever you are good at, don't run it at full brightness in every room.
- 同其塵 — join the dust. Not "become ordinary" as a strategy; simply stop holding yourself outside the conditions everyone else lives in.

These four are often read as social advice — how to avoid envy. They work better as practice: each one removes a specific kind of friction that the self generates by insisting on its own outline.

## 湛兮，似或存

Then the chapter says something odd: 湛兮，似或存 — deep and still, as if it were there, or perhaps not.

"Perhaps" is doing real work. The Dao is not asserted as an entity that exists; it is described as something that cannot be settled into existence or non-existence. Which is why the next line refuses lineage: 吾不知誰之子，象帝之先 — I don't know whose child it is; it appears before the lord.

"Before the lord" is not a claim about chronology. It means: whatever you put at the origin — a god, a first cause, a big bang — this is prior to that, not as an earlier item in the sequence, but as what makes the sequence possible.

## What a reader can do with it

The chapter gives an image and four moves, and no doctrine. The test is practical: find the place where you are running full.

Most people have one faculty they over-use — analysis, candor, charm, care. It works, so it gets turned up; turned up, it starts generating friction that looks like other people's fault. 挫其銳 is not self-reduction. It is noticing that the edge is what's cutting, and that the cut is not necessary.
